subject: Proposal: premium SLA uplift + dedicated burst capacity for renewal
messages:

To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@brightfield.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal coming up — interest in premium SLA + burst capacity

Hi Camila,

Our renewal for Brightfield's Redwood contract is up at the end of December, and procurement asked me to surface two asks before our renewal conversation: a formal premium SLA with tighter latency targets, and a short-term dedicated burst allocation for Q1 to cover a marketing-driven traffic spike (estimated peak concurrency ~180 requests/sec, sustained ~30 min bursts).

Specifically:
- Target latency SLO: 95th percentile < 150ms for text-generation requests up to 128 tokens
- Availability SLA: 99.95% with clear credit thresholds
- Dedicated burst pool for Jan–Mar with capacity to handle the above concurrency; we can tolerate a daily burst budget
- 24/7 P1 support and a named escalation contact during the burst period

Can you share what packaging and pricing options we have for this? We also need an outline of how fallbacks will work if the burst pool is saturated (model downgrade / throttling behavior).

Thanks — Taylor
Taylor Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering, Brightfield Payments

Subject: RE: Renewal — draft commercial + SLA framing for Brightfield (internal)

Camila / Lauren — following our sync notes, draft commercial approach below. This is internal only — will refine for external.

Summary proposal:
- Term: 12 months (renewal effective 2027-01-01)
- Premium SLA: Availability SLA 99.95% (monthly uptime), with credits starting at 99.9% -> credit ladder defined in SLA addendum. Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 150ms for generation requests <=128 tokens; 99th percentile < 300ms for longer requests.
- Dedicated burst pool: Jan–Mar (90 days); baseline reserved capacity to cover steady-state QPS. Burst overlay: guaranteed 200 concurrent inference slots for bursts; engineering will reserve DGX-backed instances for the window.
- Support: 24/7 P1 through Redwood Support Plus, named on-call escalation, weekly health check during Jan–Mar.
- Commercial: +20% uplift on committed monthly fee for the premium SLA, plus a fixed monthly fee for the Jan–Mar dedicated burst (TBD). Offer a one-time onboarding credit of $10k if signed before 2026-11-20.

Operational notes for Marcus / Infra:
- We need a clear fallback policy when burst pool exhausted: fallback to a compatible lower-cost model variant (same prompt contracting) + queueing for non-P1 traffic. Cache warmup plan required 48 hrs before the first major marketing burst.
- Telemetry: add 95th/99th latency dashboards for Brightfield and enable token-level cost logging.

Attachments: redwood-billing-estimate-2027.xlsx (pricing scenarios)

Please review and flag any technical constraints. If this looks good, Camila can send a proposal and SLA addendum to Taylor.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@brightfield.com>

Hi Taylor — thanks for the detailed ask and for the call yesterday. Attached is our proposed SLA addendum and a billing estimate that covers the premium SLA uplift and the Jan–Mar dedicated burst pool. Highlights:

- SLA: 99.95% availability with a credit ladder; latency SLO 95th < 150ms for generation requests <=128 tokens.
- Burst: Guaranteed 200 concurrent inference slots for a three-month window (Jan 1–Mar 31, 2027). Included: warmup plan and a named escalation engineer during major events.
- Commercial: 18% uplift on current committed monthly fee (we applied a promotional onboarding credit of $10k). The attached spreadsheet shows three commitment bands; pick the band that best aligns with your expected usage and I’ll lock pricing.
- Next steps: If this matches what procurement needs, I can circulate the SLA addendum via DocuSign. Procurement sign-off typically takes 3–7 business days.

Attachments:
- RF-2026-BF-0912_SLA_Proposal_v2.pdf (SLA addendum with credit ladder)
- redwood-billing-estimate-2027.xlsx (pricing scenarios)

Would you like me to include a clause for an automatic fallback model downgrade order (to avoid full rejects) or would you prefer to handle throttling at the application layer? We can add the language either way.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
